introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
enonce_intro_markdown: The points $P$ and $Q$ have position vectors $\mathbf p=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf q=8\mathbf i+5\mathbf j$ respectively.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Find the vector equation of the line $l_1$ from $P$ to $Q$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A line through the point with position vector $\mathbf p$ and direction $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ has equation $\mathbf r=\mathbf p+s\,\overrightarrow{PQ}$.

$$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf q-\mathbf p=(8\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)-(2\mathbf i+\mathbf j)=6\mathbf i+4\mathbf j.$$

So

$$l_1:\ \mathbf r=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+s(6\mathbf i+4\mathbf j),$$

or, dividing the direction by $2$, $\mathbf r=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\lambda(3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)$ ($s$ and $\lambda$ are parameters).

**$l_1:\ \mathbf r=2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+s(6\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) The line $l_2$ is defined by $l_2:\ \mathbf r=\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+t(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)$. Show that the point with position vector $5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$ lies on the line $l_2$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The point lies on $l_2$ if some value of $t$ gives $5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$:

$$\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+t(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)=(1+2t)\mathbf i+(5-t)\mathbf j.$$

Equate the components:

- $\mathbf i$: $1+2t=5\Rightarrow t=2$;
- $\mathbf j$: $5-t=3\Rightarrow t=2$.

Both components give the **same** value $t=2$, so the point $5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$ lies on $l_2$. $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Find the position vector of the point of intersection of $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the point of intersection the position vectors are equal:

$$(2+6s)\mathbf i+(1+4s)\mathbf j=(1+2t)\mathbf i+(5-t)\mathbf j.$$

Equate components:

$$2+6s=1+2t\quad(1),\qquad 1+4s=5-t\quad(2).$$

From (2): $t=4-4s$. Substitute in (1): $2+6s=1+2(4-4s)=9-8s$, so $14s=7$ and $s=\dfrac12$. Then $t=4-2=2$.

Position vector (using $l_1$ with $s=\frac12$): $2\mathbf i+\mathbf j+\tfrac12(6\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)=5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$.

Check with $l_2$, $t=2$: $\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+2(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j)=5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$ ✓.

**The lines meet at the point with position vector $5\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$** (the same point as in part (b)).
